name: The three states and the fourth (waking, dream, deep sleep, turīya)

definitions.definition: The self has four quarters: vaiśvānara (waking, outward-knowing, enjoyer of the gross), taijasa (dream, inward-knowing, enjoyer of the subtle), prājña (deep sleep, become one, mass of cognition, enjoyer of bliss) and the fourth, described by negation and as the stilling of the world, auspicious and non-dual.
Not knowing inward, outward or both, not a mass of cognition, not knowing, not unknowing; unseen, not to be dealt with, non-dual; it is the self and is to be known; it is without measure.

name: The measures of Oṃ (a, u, m)

definitions.definition: The self as the syllable: a is vaiśvānara, u is taijasa, m is prājña; the fourth is without measure; the quarters are the measures and the measures the quarters.
First quarter of the self, whose field is waking; identified with the letter a.

name: Ātman is brahman (as stated in the Māṇḍūkya)

definitions.definition: "All this is brahman; this self is brahman."
